content.text:
I dug into both the installed skill/agent files **and** the Claude Code binary itself (`~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.251`), which contains the actual Zod schemas with `.describe()` docstrings. That settles several questions the installed files alone can't.

---

# 1. SKILL.md frontmatter — the real schema

**Source of truth:** the frontmatter validator embedded in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.251`. Skills and slash commands share one schema (base + extension). Extracted verbatim:

```js
// base (shared by skills and commands)
name:        "Display name. Defaults to the filename without extension."
description: "One-line summary shown in listings and the Skill tool."
model:       "Model override (`haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `fable`, or a full ID).
              Use `inherit` to match the parent conversation."
"allowed-tools":    "Tools available to the model while this file is active.
                     Comma-separated string or YAML list."
"disallowed-tools": "...Cleared when the user sends the next message."
disallowedTools:    "Canonical (normalized) alias of `disallowed-tools`."
"argument-hint":    "Placeholder text shown after the slash command name."
arguments:          "@internal — typed variant of argument-hint"
"disable-model-invocation": "If true, the model cannot invoke this via the Skill tool;
                             only users can type the slash command."
"user-invocable":   "If false, hides the slash command from users; only the model can
                     invoke it via the Skill tool."
effort:      "Thinking effort for the model: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`, or an integer."
shell:       "Shell for `!`-command blocks: `bash` or `powershell`."
version:     "@internal — bookkeeping, not surfaced to users"

// skill extension
when_to_use: "Guidance for when the model should reach for this skill.
              Becomes part of the tool description."
paths:       "Glob patterns this skill applies to. The skill only loads when the
              model touches matching files."
hooks:       "Hooks registered while this skill is active. Same shape as settings.json `hooks`."
context:     enum ["inline","fork"] — "Where the skill runs: `inline` expands into the
              current conversation; `fork` spawns a subagent."
agent:       "Agent type to spawn when `context: fork`."
background:  "Only for `context: fork`. Forks run as background agents that report back as
              a task notification instead of blocking the turn; set `false` to keep the
              caller waiting for the result in-line."
metadata:    "Free-form map for the skill author's own use... Preserved on the loaded skill."
fallback / created_by / improved_by / mcpServers / lspServers / agents / outputStyles /
themes / workflows / channels / monitors / settings / userConfig / defaultEnabled /
experimental / dependencies / displayName / author / homepage / repository / license /
keywords   → all marked "@internal"
```

Direct answers:

| Key | Real? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `model:` | **Yes** | Aliases `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`/`fable`, full IDs (`claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `…[1m]` for 1M-context), or `inherit`. |
| `allowed-tools:` | **Yes** | Comma-string or YAML list. Plus `disallowed-tools`. |
| `disable-model-invocation:` | **Yes** | Makes the skill user-typed-only. |
| `context:` | **Yes** | `inline` (default) or `fork`. Confirmed default: `Emt(e,t,r){return e.getContext?.(t,r) ?? e.context ?? "inline"}` |
| `effort:` | **Yes** — undocumented but real | Validated against `Uh=["low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]` plus integers. Note the `.describe()` text omits `xhigh`; the validator accepts it. Invalid values log `Skill ${r} has invalid effort '${x}'`. |

**Keys that are NOT harness keys.** The Vercel plugin skills use `chainTo:`, `validate:`, `retrieval:`, `upgradeToSkill:`. `grep`ping the binary: `chainTo` → **0 occurrences**, `upgradeToSkill` → **0 occurrences**. Those are Vercel's own conventions read by Vercel's own hooks, not the harness. Don't copy them.

Representative real frontmatter on this machine:

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/contentful-register-component/SKILL.md`
```yaml
---
name: contentful-register-component
description: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
allowed-tools: Read, Edit, Bash
---
```

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/1.0.0/commands/ralph-loop.md` (a command, showing the shared schema plus `hide-from-slash-command-tool`, which appears in the binary's key-union list):
```yaml
---
description: "Start Ralph Loop in current session"
argument-hint: "PROMPT [--max-iterations N] [--completion-promise TEXT]"
allowed-tools: ["Bash(${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/setup-ralph-loop.sh:*)"]
hide-from-slash-command-tool: "true"
---
```

---

# 2. Can a skill change the model of the CURRENT session? — **Yes, per-turn.**

This is the headline finding, and it contradicts the usual "model is session-level" advice.

The Skill tool's `call()` returns **context layers**:

```js
let nn=[];
if (pe.length>0) nn.push({kind:"allowed_tools", allowedTools:pe});
if (ge)          nn.push({kind:"model",  mainLoopModel: W8e(ge, r.options.mainLoopModel)});
if (Ce!==void 0) nn.push({kind:"effort", effort: Ce});
return { data:{success:!0, commandName:C, ...}, newMessages:en, ...nn.length>0 && {contextLayers:nn} }
```

And those layers are what the request builder reads — last-layer-wins:

```js
function c(e){ let o=e.options?.mainLoopModel;
  for (let t of e.permissionLayers??[]) if (t.kind==="model") o=t.mainLoopModel;
  return o }

function Djt(e){ let o; for (let t of e) if (t.kind==="effort") o=t.effort; return o }
function tu(e){ return Djt(e.permissionLayers) ?? il(e.getAppState(), c(e)) }
```

So `model:` + `effort:` in a SKILL.md **do** re-target the main loop model and effort of the session that invoked the skill.

**Scope and caveats — all confirmed in the binary:**

- It is **turn-scoped, not persistent.** From an internal comment: *"Turn-scoped divergence is accepted: a turn running under a skill/command frontmatter model override compacts against that model's window while the frame keeps the resting model's."* The session's "resting model" is unchanged; `/model`, the statusline, and the next user message go back to it.
- Guardrail: `W8e()` — if the requested model isn't in the `availableModels` allowlist, it warns ``Skill/command model "${e}" is not in the availableModels allowlist; keeping the session model`` and no switch happens.
- **`context: fork` does NOT change the caller's model.** The fork branch returns *before* the `contextLayers` block:
  `if (B?.type==="prompt" && Emt(B,t||"",r)==="fork" && !M) { return await eIn(...) }`
  Instead, the model/effort are handed to the spawned subagent (`Bb({... model: fn, permissionLayers: [{kind:"effort", effort}] ...})`).

**So for your stated goal — "skill X on Opus 5 at max effort, skill Y on Sonnet 5 at max effort" — you have two real designs:**

```yaml
# A) inline: hijacks the current session's model+effort for the rest of the turn
---
name: deep-architect
description: ...
model: claude-opus-5
effort: max
---

# B) fork: runs in an isolated subagent on that model/effort; session untouched
---
name: bulk-refactor
description: ...
context: fork
model: claude-sonnet-5
effort: max
background: false      # keep the caller waiting for the result inline
---
```

Both are genuinely supported. (B) is the cleaner one if you don't want the caller's model silently mutated mid-turn.

**Everything else that controls model, ranked by real precedence** (from `aJn()`, the startup resolver):

1. CLI `--model` → source `"cli"`
2. Agent frontmatter `model:` (when the agent is the *main* session, via `--agent`) → source `"agent_frontmatter"`
3. `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` env var → source `"env"`
4. `settings.model` (policy > project > user) → yours is `"model": "claude-opus-5"` in `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/settings.json`

Then, *during* the session: `/model` (a `set_model` control request — *"Model to switch to. Omitted, null, or 'default' resets to the session default model"*), and skill/command frontmatter layers on top of that.

**Effort specifically:**
- `settings.effortLevel: enum ["low","medium","high","xhigh"]` — *"Persisted effort level for supported models."* Yours is `"effortLevel": "xhigh"`.
- `settings.modelSettings: { "<model-id>": { effortLevel } }` — **per-model persisted effort**. This is the settings-level way to say "Opus at xhigh, Sonnet at xhigh" without any skill involvement.
- Note the asymmetry: settings only accept up to `xhigh`; skill/agent frontmatter `effort:` also accepts `max` and raw integers.

Other real env vars found: `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU,FABLE}_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT`, `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS`.

---

# 3. Subagent (`.claude/agents/*.md`) frontmatter — full schema

There are **no agents installed under `~/.claude/agents/`** (the directory doesn't exist) and none in your projects — only plugin agents. But the binary has the complete schema:

```js
name:        "Agent identifier. Required — this is how the Agent tool and `--agent` flag address it."
description: "When to use this agent. Required — shown in the Agent tool listing."
model:       "Model override for this agent. Use `inherit` to match the spawning conversation."
tools:       "Tools available to this agent. Replaces the default set."
disallowedTools: "Tools removed from the default set. Ignored if `tools` is set."
color:       "@internal — display color in the agents UI"
effort:      "Thinking effort: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`, or an integer."
permissionMode: "Permission mode the agent runs in."
mcpServers:  "MCP servers to connect when this agent runs."
hooks:       "Hooks registered while this agent runs."
maxTurns:    "Maximum conversation turns before the agent stops."
skills:      "Skills preloaded for this agent."
initialPrompt: "Auto-submitted first message when this agent runs as the main session
                (via `--agent` or settings). Not read when spawned as a subagent."
memory:      "Memory scope: `user`, `project`, or `local`."
background:  "If true, the agent runs in the background by default."
isolation:   "Filesystem isolation: `worktree` runs in a temporary git worktree."
observer:    "Agent type auto-spawned as a background observer whenever this agent runs."
observerMessage: "Supplemental postamble appended ... to each activity digest sent to the observer."
observeSubagents: "If false, subagents this agent spawns do not inherit its observer. Defaults to true."
experimental: { cacheTtl: 'Prompt cache TTL for this agent\'s requests ("5m" or "1h")...' }
```

**Yes — a subagent can be pinned to a specific model AND an effort level.** Live proof, `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/claude-security/agents/explore.md`:

```yaml
---
name: explore
description: Read-only code explorer that the plugin's other agents dispatch to map a codebase — locate files, trace how a flow is wired, find every caller of a symbol, answer "where does X happen".
model: sonnet
effort: xhigh
color: cyan
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash
---
```

and the orchestrator, `.../claude-security/agents/claude-security.md`:

```yaml
---
name: claude-security
description: 'The dedicated Claude Security orchestrator. ...'
model: opus
effort: xhigh
color: purple
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion, Workflow, Workflow(claude-security:scan), TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskList, TaskUpdate, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Agent(claude-security:scan-inventory, claude-security:scan-researcher, claude-security:scan-verifier, claude-security:patch-generator, claude-security:patch-verifier, claude-security:explore)
initialPrompt: "/claude-security:claude-security"
---
```

Note `tools:` supports **scoped grants** — `Agent(a, b, c)` and `Workflow(name)` — restricting *which* subagents an agent may dispatch. `orange`/`purple` are used as colors, so `color` isn't limited to the six the plugin-dev docs list (it's `@internal` and free-form).

**Correction to the plugin-dev docs.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/plugin-dev/*/skills/agent-development/SKILL.md` claims `model` and `color` are **required** and lists only `name/description/model/color/tools`. Both claims are wrong against this binary — everything except `name` and `description` is `.optional()`, and `effort`, `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `memory`, `isolation`, `observer`, `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `initialPrompt`, `background`, `experimental.cacheTtl` all exist. That skill is stale; trust the schema.

**The Agent tool's runtime `model` parameter** (verbatim):

```js
description:   "A short (3-5 word) description of the task"
prompt:        "The task for the agent to perform"
subagent_type: "The type of specialized agent to use for this task"
model: enum ["sonnet","opus","haiku","fable"] —
  "Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's
   model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent
   definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent
   model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: 'fork'…"
```

**There is no `effort` parameter on the Agent tool.** `effort` appears in exactly two Zod schemas in the whole binary — skill/command frontmatter and agent frontmatter. So: **effort is only settable declaratively (an `.md` file) or at session level — never at spawn time.** If you want "Sonnet at max effort," you must write an agent file or a skill file; you cannot get it from `Agent({model:"sonnet", ...})`.

---

# 4. Skill-to-skill handoff — yes, and it's first-class

**Nested `Skill` calls are explicitly supported.** From the Skill tool's `call()`:

```js
let A = r.options.activeSkill;              // save the outer skill
let x = A ?? r.options.spawnedBySkill;
r.options.activeSkill = C;                  // enter the inner skill
try { ... } finally { if (M || !F) r.options.activeSkill = A; }   // restore
```

The save/restore of `activeSkill` exists precisely because a skill can invoke another skill. Attribution is threaded through as `spawnedBySkill` / `spawnedByForkedSkill` for telemetry.

**Declarative chaining** is `context: fork` + `agent:` — a skill whose entire body runs as a named subagent, with its own model, effort, tools, and optionally `background: true` (returns as a task notification instead of blocking).

**Instructional chaining** (a skill telling the model to spawn subagents) is the dominant installed pattern:

- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.3.0/skills/subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md` — "dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end."
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.3.0/skills/dispatching-parallel-agents/SKILL.md`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/skill-creator/skills/skill-creator/` — ships an **`agents/` subdirectory inside the skill directory** (`grader.md`, `comparator.md`, `analyzer.md`) and instructs: *"The agents/ directory contains instructions for specialized subagents. Read them when you need to spawn the relevant subagent."* These are prompt bodies read and pasted into a generic subagent, not registered agent types.
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.3.0/skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md` documents a **priority convention** for skill chaining: *"When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills carry it out."*

One real constraint found: in **coordinator mode**, skills with `disable-model-invocation` can't be run — *"the coordinator does not load skill content, and workers cannot invoke it via the Skill tool."*

---

# 5. Loop mechanics — `loop` vs `ralph-loop`

These are architecturally opposite. **`ralph-loop` is what you want for build-verify-score-revise.**

### `ralph-loop` — Stop-hook loop with a state file

Files: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/1.0.0/{hooks/hooks.json,hooks/stop-hook.sh,scripts/setup-ralph-loop.sh,commands/ralph-loop.md}`

- **Iteration:** a `Stop` hook that refuses to let the session end. It emits `{"decision":"block","reason":"<the original prompt>","systemMessage":"🔄 Ralph iteration N | …"}`, which re-injects the *same* prompt as the next user turn. Same session, same context, same model.
- **State:** `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` — markdown with YAML frontmatter, written by `setup-ralph-loop.sh`:
  ```yaml
  ---
  active: true
  iteration: 1
  session_id: ${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}
  max_iterations: $MAX_ITERATIONS
  completion_promise: $COMPLETION_PROMISE_YAML
  started_at: "…"
  ---
  $PROMPT
  ```
  The hook re-reads it every stop, increments `iteration:` via `sed` into a temp file + atomic `mv`. Session-isolated: if `session_id` doesn't match the hook's `session_id`, the hook exits 0 and doesn't touch the file.
- **Stopping conditions — exactly three:**
  1. `iteration >= max_iterations` (when `max_iterations > 0`)
  2. The last assistant **text** block contains `<promise>EXACT TEXT</promise>` matching `completion_promise` (extracted with `perl -0777`, whitespace-normalized, compared with `=` not `==` to avoid glob matching)
  3. A corrupt/unparseable state file, missing transcript, or jq failure — all of which `rm` the state file and exit
  There is **no manual stop**: *"⚠️ WARNING: This loop cannot be stopped manually! It will run infinitely unless you set --max-iterations or --completion-promise."*
- **How it reads its own progress:** it doesn't summarize — it re-runs the same prompt and lets the model observe the filesystem and git history. The last assistant text block is parsed from `transcript_path` (capped at the last 100 assistant JSONL lines).
- Heavy anti-cheat prompting against lying to escape: *"Do NOT output false statements to exit the loop… Do not force it by lying."*

### `loop` — a bundled scheduler skill, not an iteration harness

Implemented in JS inside the binary (no SKILL.md on disk). Two modes:

- **Fixed interval** (`/loop 5m /foo`, or trailing `every 20m`): parses to a cron expression and calls **`CronCreate`** with `recurring: true`, then executes the prompt once immediately. Cancel with `CronDelete`; recurring tasks auto-expire after a fixed number of days (stated in the confirmation).
- **Dynamic / self-paced** (`/loop <prompt>`, no interval): at the end of each turn the model calls **`ScheduleWakeup`** with `delaySeconds` (*"Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime"*), `reason`, `prompt` (the original `/loop …` input verbatim, so the next firing re-enters the skill), and `noop`. Optionally arms a **`Monitor`** with `persistent: true` so events arrive as `<task-notification>` and wake the loop early — `delaySeconds` then becomes a fallback heartbeat (guidance: 1200–1800s).
- **State:** `~/.claude/loop.md` or `<project>/.claude/loop.md` (a task list, mapped internally as `["loop-file","loop.md"]`). A sentinel prompt expands at fire time to the full file contents on the first delivery or whenever `loop.md` changed, and to a short reminder otherwise.
- **Stopping:** `ScheduleWakeup({stop:true})` (returns `cancelledWakeups`; note *"a recurring /loop cron is not cancelled by stop:true"*), or `CronDelete` for the cron, or simply not re-arming — *"re-arming is a per-turn choice, not a default."*

### Which for build-verify-score-revise

**`ralph-loop`.** The cycle needs (a) tight, back-to-back iterations with no wall-clock gap, (b) full accumulated context across iterations, and (c) a semantic exit condition. Ralph gives all three: the Stop hook fires immediately, context is continuous, and `--completion-promise 'ALL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA PASS'` + `--max-iterations N` is exactly a score-gated exit.

`/loop` is a *scheduler* — minimum 60s between wakeups, designed for polling external state (deploys, PRs, CI), with each firing a fresh turn. It's wrong for a tight revise cycle.

Two things to design around with Ralph:
- The re-injected prompt is byte-identical every iteration, so **your prompt must self-orient** ("read `SCORE.md`, find the lowest-scoring criterion, fix only that, re-run the scorer, rewrite `SCORE.md`"). Ralph's own state file holds only `iteration` — your score/ledger needs its own file.
- The completion promise is compared by exact string match against `<promise>…</promise>`, so make the phrase unambiguous and only-true-when-true.

---

# 6. Where skills live, discovery, and precedence

**Discovery roots** — the exact log line the binary emits:

```
Loading skills from: managed=${o}, user=${r}, project=[${u.join(", ")}]
```
where `r = <configDir>/skills` (→ `~/.claude/skills`), `o = <managedDir>/.claude/skills`, and project dirs come from the workspace resolver.

**Load order within skill directories** (from the same function, `me = […]`):

1. **managed / policy** — `policySettings` (disable with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_POLICY_SKILLS`)
2. **user** — `~/.claude/skills` (`userSettings`)
3. **synced skills** — cloud-synced; explicitly dropped on collision: `` [skills] dropping synced skill '${name}': a local skill owns that name ``
4. **project** — `<project>/.claude/skills`
5. additional workspace dirs — `<dir>/.claude/skills`
6. `.claude/commands`

**Then the global merge** (`F = [...]`, first-wins by name):

**skill-dir skills → workflows → plugin skills → bundled skills → builtin plugin skills**

Confirmed by a changelog entry in the binary: *"Fixed bundled skill aliases like `/checkup` and `/review` reporting 'Unknown command' … when a user or project skill shadows the bundled skill."* So **your `~/.claude/skills/` beats any plugin skill and any bundled skill of the same name.** Name resolution is exact-match-first, alias/unqualified-name fallback second (`ua()`).

**Collision handling is namespacing, not silent shadowing.** When a project skill collides with an unscoped name, the harness renames it `<dir>:<name>` and rewrites the description:

```js
`scoped to ${t}/ — use this instead of the unscoped "${e.name}" skill when the files
 being changed are under ${t}/`
// non-colliding project skills instead get:
`from ${t}/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under ${t}/`
```

You can see this happening live in this very session: your `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/code-review/` surfaces as **`zimmermann-pwa:code-review`** alongside the unscoped bundled `code-review`, with exactly that generated suffix.

**Other discovery facts:**
- Skills with `paths:` are **conditional** — held back until the model touches a matching file, then activated.
- Same-file dedupe by content hash: `Skipping duplicate skill '${name}' from ${source} (same file already loaded from ${…})`.
- Per-skill visibility knob in settings: `skillOverrides: { "<name>": "on" | "name-only" | "user-invocable-only" | "off" }` — *"'name-only' lists the skill without its description; 'user-invocable-only' hides it from the model but keeps /name; 'off' hides it from both."*
- `disableBundledSkills: true` (or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS=1`) — *"Plugins, .claude/skills/, and .claude/commands/ are unaffected."*
- Plugin skills also load from a plugin's `skills/`, and the Figma plugin additionally uses `workflow-skills/` (`.../figma/2.2.95/workflow-skills/…`) — that path is plugin-specific, not a general convention.

---

# Genuinely undeterminable from local files

- **Exact lifetime boundary of a `{kind:"model"}` layer.** I can prove it's set on the tool-use context and read per-request (last-wins), and there's an explicit "turn-scoped" comment plus "Cleared when the user sends the next message" on the sibling `disallowed-tools` key. Whether *every* layer kind is dropped at the identical moment is a runtime behavior I can't confirm without executing a skill — which is out of scope here.
- **Whether `effort: max` is accepted by your account/model tier.** `max` is in `Uh` and passes validation, but `settings.effortLevel` only enumerates up to `xhigh`, and there's entitlement-gating machinery (`per_turn_effort` capability, `default_effort`). Local files can't tell you what your account actually permits.
- **The cron auto-expiry day count** for `/loop` fixed-interval mode — the template string is `recurring tasks auto-expire after ${NX} days` and I couldn't resolve `NX` reliably from the stripped bundle.
- **The `color:` value set.** It's `@internal` with no enum in the schema; installed agents use `orange` and `purple` beyond the six the plugin-dev docs list, so the docs' list is not authoritative — but I can't enumerate the real set.
